In the mathematical theory of probability, '''offered load''' is a concept in queuing theory. The offered load is a measure of traffic in a queue. The offered load is given by [[Little's law]]: the arrival rate into the queue (symbolized with [[lambda|λ]]) multiplied by the mean holding time (symbolized by [[Tau|τ]]), equals the average amount of time spent by items in the queue. Offered load is expressed in [[Erlang unit]]s or [[call-second]]s per hour,<ref>{{cite book | title = Fundamentals of Telecommunications | url = https://archive.org/details/fundamentalstele00free | url-access = limited | page = [https://archive.org/details/fundamentalstele00free/page/n83 57] | first = Roger L. | last = Freeman | publisher = John Wiley | year = 2005 | isbn = 0471710458}}</ref> a dimensionless measure.
